rationale: All three describe activation/increase of TGF-beta signaling pathway using different wording.
Both involve TGF-beta but one describes activation of the latent form (upstream ligand activation) while the other describes pathway-level activation, which are distinct processes.
Collagen deposition is a cellular/ECM process while lung fibrosis is an organ-level pathological outcome in a specific tissue context.
Both target mitochondrial complex III but one describes binding of an inhibitor and the other describes functional inhibition, which are distinct processes.
Both target mitochondrial complex IV but one describes binding and the other describes functional inhibition.
Both target mitochondrial complex V but one describes binding and the other describes functional inhibition.
Both describe decreased/reduced mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation using different wording.

Decrease in coupling of oxidative phosphorylation and decreased mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation describe related but distinct aspects of the same process — coupling efficiency vs. overall activity.
Both describe increased DNA damage/strand breaks; 'Increase, DNA damage' and 'Increase, DNA strand breaks' are effectively synonymous at this level of description.
Both describe DNA strand breaks but one specifies double-strand breaks specifically while the other is general DNA strand breaks.
Both measure reproductive success but in strictly opposite directions — one increased and one decreased.
Both measure population size/trajectory but in opposite directions — increased population vs. population decline.
Both measure triiodothyronine (T3) in tissues but in opposite directions — decreased vs. increased.
Both describe activation of CYP2E1 using slightly different wording.

Opening of calcium channels causing calcium influx and increase in cytosolic calcium describe the same upstream-to-downstream event closely enough to be considered the same KE in many AOP contexts; both describe intracellular calcium increase resulting from channel opening.

Blockade of L-type calcium channels and decrease in calcium currents describe related but distinct events — one is the molecular initiating event (channel blockade) and the other is the resulting electrophysiological change.
Both involve microtubules but one describes binding of stabilizing agents and the other describes disruption of dynamic instability, which are distinct processes sharing the same biological object.
Both involve glutathione but synthesis (production process) and homeostasis (balance/maintenance) are distinct biological processes sharing the same object.
Both describe decreased ATP production/pool using different wording — 'Decrease, ATP production' and 'Decrease, Adenosine triphosphate pool' refer to the same biological endpoint.
Both describe general apoptosis without context-specific qualifiers.
Oocyte apoptosis specifies a cell-type context while general apoptosis does not, making them similar events in different biological contexts.

Decreased apoptosis in epithelial cells is directionally opposite and context-specific compared to general apoptosis increase; these share the same process in different biological contexts and directions.
Both describe reduction/decrease in growth using slightly different wording.
HDAC inhibition and increased histone acetylation are causally linked but represent distinct biological events — inhibition of the enzyme vs. the resulting epigenetic mark increase.
Hepatocytotoxicity and liver injury both describe hepatic toxicity/damage at the organ level using different terminology.
Inhibition of mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma and depletion of mtDNA are causally linked but represent distinct biological events — enzyme inhibition vs. resulting mtDNA loss.

SP (Substance P) release and increased neurokinin A are related neuropeptides but these are distinct molecules; however, 1222 describes local SP increase which is a merge candidate only with itself — keeping separate from NKA.
Both describe neuronal release of neuropeptides (CGRP and Substance P respectively) in the context of trigeminal nerve activation but involve different molecules.
Binding to topoisomerase II and DNA double-strand breaks are causally related but represent distinct biological processes — enzyme binding vs. resulting DNA damage.
Both involve fibroblasts but differentiation and activation are distinct cellular processes.
Decreased cardiac contractility and decreased cardiac ejection fraction are causally related but represent distinct physiological measurements of cardiac function.
Decrease in photosynthesis and decrease in light harvest capacity are related but distinct steps in the photosynthetic process.
Both describe glycolysis but in opposite directions — decrease vs. increase.
Decrease in oogenesis and increase in follicular atresia both relate to reduced female reproductive output but describe distinct biological processes.
Increased oocyte maturation and induced spawning are related reproductive events but describe distinct biological processes in a sequential pathway.

Increased transcription of acute phase protein genes and systemic acute phase response are causally linked but represent distinct biological events — gene expression vs. systemic physiological response.
Mu opioid receptor agonism and release of G proteins share the same receptor but describe distinct sequential events — receptor activation vs. downstream G protein signaling.
Serotonin 1A receptor agonism and anti-depressant activity are causally linked but represent distinct biological events — receptor-level vs. behavioral/pharmacological outcome.
TRPA1 activation and opening of calcium channels/calcium influx are causally linked sequential events but represent distinct biological processes.
Decrease in leaf cell mitosis and decrease in leaf development are causally related but represent distinct biological events — cellular division vs. organ-level development.
Increased depression and decreased neuroplasticity are related but distinct biological events in the same pathway context.
Decreased calcium binding to Troponin C and decreased cardiac contractility are causally sequential but represent distinct molecular vs. physiological events.
Reduced neural crest cell migration and reduced collagen production are distinct biological events that both contribute to craniofacial developmental defects.
Both measure cell proliferation but in opposite directions — increase (epithelial cells) vs. decrease.
Increase in epithelial cell proliferation and induction of persistent/sustained proliferation describe similar events but one is cell-type specific and the other is general/persistent.
